answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because copper only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
